title: Teeth Whitening
description: In-clinic brightening for a visibly whiter smile in one visit.
details:
Professional whitening lifts stains from tea, coffee, paan, smoking and age. A dentist-applied whitening gel is used with your gums protected, so results are faster, more even and safer than over-the-counter kits.

Ideal for: Yellow or dull teeth from tea, coffee or smoking; A brighter smile before a wedding or event; Healthy teeth and gums with no active decay.

What happens: 1) Check-up and shade recording to confirm whitening is suitable 2) Polishing to remove surface plaque 3) Gums protected with a barrier gel 4) Whitening gel applied and activated in short cycles 5) Final shade check and aftercare advice

Time: About 60–90 minutes · Visits: Usually 1 · Recovery: Mild temporary sensitivity for 24–48 hours is normal

Aftercare: Avoid tea, coffee, colas and paan for 48 hours; Use a sensitivity toothpaste if teeth feel tender; Touch-up sessions keep results longer.

title: Dental Implants
description: Permanent, natural-looking replacements for missing teeth.
details:
An implant is a small titanium post placed in the jawbone that acts like a tooth root. Once it fuses with the bone, a crown is fixed on top. Implants don't rely on neighbouring teeth, help preserve bone and can last for many years with good care.

Ideal for: One or more missing teeth; Loose or uncomfortable dentures; Adults with good general health and enough jawbone.

What happens: 1) Consultation, examination and X-rays to assess bone 2) Implant placed under local anaesthetic 3) Healing period while the implant fuses with bone 4) Abutment and custom crown fitted 5) Bite check and long-term review

Time: About 1 hour per implant for placement · Visits: 2–4 visits over roughly 3–6 months · Recovery: Mild swelling or soreness for a few days

Aftercare: Soft foods for the first few days; Brush and floss around the implant like a natural tooth; Avoid smoking — it slows healing.

title: Root Canal Treatment (RCT)
description: Comfortable root canal treatment with modern rotary instruments.
details:
When the nerve inside a tooth becomes infected or inflamed, root canal treatment removes the infection, cleans and shapes the canals, and seals them. It relieves pain and saves the natural tooth. Most teeth then need a crown for protection.

Ideal for: Severe or lingering toothache; Pain on biting or sensitivity to hot drinks; Swelling or a gum boil near a tooth.

What happens: 1) X-ray and diagnosis 2) Local anaesthetic so the procedure is comfortable 3) Infected nerve removed; canals cleaned and shaped 4) Canals disinfected and sealed 5) Tooth restored, usually with a crown

Time: 60–90 minutes · Visits: 1–2 (single-visit where suitable) · Recovery: Mild tenderness for a few days

Aftercare: Avoid chewing hard food on the tooth until it is crowned; Take pain relief as advised.

title: Teeth Cleaning & Scaling
description: Removes tartar and stains to keep gums healthy and breath fresh.
details:
Even with good brushing, hard tartar builds up where a toothbrush can't reach. Ultrasonic scaling and polishing removes tartar and surface stains, reduces bleeding gums and bad breath, and helps prevent gum disease.

Ideal for: Bleeding gums when brushing; Bad breath or visible tartar; Everyone — every 6 months.

What happens: 1) Gum and tooth check 2) Ultrasonic scaling to remove tartar 3) Hand scaling for fine deposits 4) Polishing and brushing advice

Time: 30–45 minutes · Visits: 1 · Recovery: None

Aftercare: Brush twice daily for 2 minutes; Clean between teeth daily.

title: Braces & Clear Aligners
description: Metal, ceramic and clear aligner options to straighten teeth.
details:
Orthodontic treatment gradually moves teeth into better positions to improve appearance, bite and ease of cleaning. Metal braces are the most economical; ceramic braces are tooth-coloured; clear aligners are nearly invisible and removable.

Ideal for: Crooked, crowded or gapped teeth; Overbite, underbite or crossbite; Teens and adults.

What happens: 1) Orthodontic consultation, photos and X-rays 2) Treatment plan and option selection 3) Braces fitted or first aligners given 4) Adjustment visits every 4–6 weeks 5) Retainers to hold the result

Time: Typically 12–24 months of treatment · Visits: Regular check-ups every 4–6 weeks · Recovery: Mild soreness for a few days after adjustments

Aftercare: Avoid hard and sticky foods with braces; Wear aligners 20–22 hours a day; Wear retainers as instructed.

title: Emergency Dental Care
description: Same-day relief for toothache, swelling and broken teeth.
details:
Dental pain can't wait. Call us and we'll do our best to see you the same day for severe toothache, facial swelling, broken or knocked-out teeth, lost fillings or crowns, and bleeding after an extraction.

Ideal for: Severe toothache; Swelling of the face or gums; Broken, chipped or knocked-out tooth.

What happens: 1) Call the clinic for a same-day slot 2) Quick assessment and X-ray 3) Pain relief and urgent treatment 4) Plan for any follow-up treatment

Time: 30–60 minutes · Visits: 1, plus follow-up if needed · Recovery: Depends on the problem

Aftercare: Knocked-out tooth: keep it in milk and come in immediately; Facial swelling with fever or difficulty swallowing: seek urgent care.

title: Dental Bonding
description: Tooth-coloured resin to repair chips, gaps and uneven edges.
details:
Composite bonding uses tooth-coloured resin that is shaped directly on the tooth and hardened with a light. It's a quick, conservative way to fix small chips, close minor gaps and even out edges — usually without drilling or anaesthetic.

Ideal for: Chipped or cracked front teeth; Small gaps between teeth; Uneven or worn edges.

What happens: 1) Shade matched to your natural teeth 2) Tooth surface lightly prepared 3) Resin applied, sculpted and light-cured 4) Shaped and polished to a natural finish

Time: 30–60 minutes per tooth · Visits: Usually 1 · Recovery: None — eat and smile normally the same day

Aftercare: Avoid biting hard objects (nails, ice, pens); Limit staining drinks in the first 48 hours.

title: Cosmetic Dentistry & Smile Makeover
description: A planned combination of treatments to redesign your smile.
details:
A smile makeover combines whitening, bonding, crowns, gum contouring or orthodontics into one plan built around your face, lips and goals. We discuss what you'd like to change, show you the options and agree a step-by-step plan before starting.

Ideal for: Several cosmetic concerns at once (colour, shape, gaps); Old, discoloured fillings or crowns on front teeth; Anyone wanting a confident smile for photos and events.

What happens: 1) Smile consultation, photos and examination 2) Treatment options explained with a clear plan 3) Foundation work first (cleaning, gum health, fillings) 4) Cosmetic treatments carried out in planned stages 5) Final review and maintenance plan

Time: Depends on the plan · Visits: From 1 visit to several weeks · Recovery: Varies by treatment

Aftercare: Regular cleanings every 6 months; A night guard if you grind your teeth.

title: Dental Crowns
description: Strong caps that protect and restore weak or broken teeth.
details:
A crown covers the whole visible part of a tooth to restore its strength, shape and appearance. Crowns are commonly placed after root canal treatment, on heavily filled or cracked teeth, or on top of an implant. Metal-ceramic and all-ceramic options are available.

Ideal for: Teeth after root canal treatment; Cracked, broken or heavily filled teeth; Improving the shape or colour of a tooth.

What happens: 1) Tooth shaped under local anaesthetic 2) Impression or scan taken; temporary crown fitted 3) Custom crown made in the lab 4) Permanent crown checked and cemented

Time: About 60 minutes per visit · Visits: Usually 2 · Recovery: Minimal — slight sensitivity for a few days

Aftercare: Avoid sticky food on the temporary crown; Brush and floss normally.

title: Dental Bridges
description: Fixed replacement teeth anchored to neighbouring teeth.
details:
A bridge fills the gap left by a missing tooth using crowns on the teeth on either side to hold a false tooth in between. It is fixed in place — not removable — and restores chewing, speech and appearance.

Ideal for: One to three missing teeth in a row; Patients who prefer a fixed option without surgery.

What happens: 1) Supporting teeth prepared 2) Impression taken; temporary bridge fitted 3) Custom bridge made in the lab 4) Bridge checked, adjusted and cemented

Time: About 60–90 minutes per visit · Visits: Usually 2 · Recovery: Minimal

Aftercare: Use a floss threader or interdental brush under the bridge daily.

title: Complete & Partial Dentures
description: Removable teeth to restore your smile and chewing.
details:
Complete dentures replace all teeth in an arch; partial dentures fill gaps when some natural teeth remain. Each set is custom-made from impressions of your mouth for comfort, fit and a natural look.

Ideal for: Missing all or many teeth; Patients wanting an affordable replacement option; Those not ready for implants.

What happens: 1) Examination and impressions 2) Bite registration and tooth shade/shape selection 3) Try-in of wax set-up 4) Final denture fitted and adjusted 5) Follow-up adjustments for comfort

Time: 30–45 minutes per visit · Visits: Usually 3–5 · Recovery: A few weeks to get used to speaking and eating

Aftercare: Remove and clean dentures daily; Take them out at night to rest your gums; Return for relines as your gums change.

title: Dental Fillings
description: Tooth-coloured fillings to repair cavities and small breaks.
details:
When decay creates a cavity, the damaged part is removed and the tooth is rebuilt with a tooth-coloured composite filling. Treating cavities early prevents pain and avoids the need for a root canal later.

Ideal for: Cavities and decay; Small chips or worn areas; Replacing old or broken fillings.

What happens: 1) Local anaesthetic if needed 2) Decay removed and tooth cleaned 3) Composite filling placed in layers and light-cured 4) Bite checked and polished

Time: 20–45 minutes per tooth · Visits: 1 · Recovery: Eat normally once numbness wears off

Aftercare: Brush twice daily with fluoride toothpaste; Cut down on sugary snacks.

title: Tooth Extractions
description: Gentle removal of teeth that can't be saved.
details:
Sometimes a tooth is too damaged, loose or infected to save. Extraction is done under local anaesthetic, as gently as possible, and we'll talk you through options to replace the tooth afterwards.

Ideal for: Badly broken or decayed teeth; Loose teeth from advanced gum disease; Teeth removed for orthodontic treatment.

What happens: 1) Examination and X-ray 2) Local anaesthetic 3) Tooth gently loosened and removed 4) Gauze placed and aftercare explained

Time: 20–45 minutes · Visits: 1 · Recovery: 2–3 days of mild soreness

Aftercare: Bite on gauze for 30–45 minutes; No rinsing, spitting or straws for 24 hours; Soft, cool foods for the first day.

title: Wisdom Teeth Removal
description: Safe removal of painful or impacted wisdom teeth.
details:
Wisdom teeth often don't have enough room to come through properly, causing pain, swelling, infection or damage to the tooth in front. An X-ray shows their position so we can plan a simple or surgical removal.

Ideal for: Pain or swelling at the back of the jaw; Repeated gum infection around a wisdom tooth; Impacted or partially erupted wisdom teeth.

What happens: 1) X-ray to check position and roots 2) Local anaesthetic 3) Tooth removed (sometimes in sections) 4) Stitches placed if needed

Time: 30–60 minutes · Visits: 1, plus a review if stitches are placed · Recovery: 3–7 days of swelling and stiffness

Aftercare: Cold compress on the cheek for the first day; Warm salt-water rinses from day two; Avoid smoking.

title: Minor Oral Surgery
description: Surgical extractions, cyst removal and implant-related procedures.
details:
Minor oral surgery covers procedures beyond a simple extraction — such as surgical removal of broken roots, small cysts or lesions, and bone or gum procedures before implants. Everything is done under local anaesthetic with careful planning.

Ideal for: Broken roots left in the jaw; Small cysts or growths in the mouth; Preparation for implants.

What happens: 1) Examination and imaging 2) Local anaesthetic 3) Procedure 4) Stitches and review

Time: 30–90 minutes · Visits: 1–2 · Recovery: A few days to a week

Aftercare: Follow written aftercare instructions; Attend the review appointment.

title: Scaling & Root Planing (Deep Cleaning)
description: Deep cleaning below the gumline to treat gum disease.
details:
When gum disease forms pockets between the gums and teeth, deep cleaning removes tartar and bacteria from root surfaces and smooths them so the gums can heal and reattach.

Ideal for: Diagnosed gum disease (periodontitis); Deep gum pockets or receding gums; Loose teeth from gum problems.

What happens: 1) Gum pocket measurements 2) Local anaesthetic for comfort 3) Deep cleaning of roots, one section at a time 4) Review after 6–8 weeks

Time: 45–60 minutes per session · Visits: Usually 2–4 · Recovery: Gums may be tender for a few days

Aftercare: Antiseptic mouthwash if prescribed; Very thorough daily cleaning.

title: Periodontal Maintenance
description: Regular gum care visits to keep gum disease under control.
details:
After gum disease treatment, more frequent maintenance cleanings — typically every 3–4 months — keep bacteria under control and protect the supporting bone around your teeth.

Ideal for: Patients previously treated for gum disease.

What happens: 1) Gum check and measurements 2) Targeted cleaning 3) Home-care review

Time: 45 minutes · Visits: Every 3–4 months · Recovery: None

Aftercare: Keep up daily interdental cleaning.

title: Preventive Dentistry
description: Check-ups, fluoride and sealants to stop problems early.
details:
Prevention is the most affordable dentistry. Regular check-ups catch decay and gum problems early, and fluoride varnish or fissure sealants protect children's and adults' teeth from cavities.

Ideal for: Children and teenagers; Anyone prone to cavities; Families wanting regular care.

What happens: 1) Examination 2) Cleaning 3) Fluoride or sealants if needed 4) Personal home-care advice

Time: 30 minutes · Visits: Every 6 months · Recovery: None

Aftercare: Limit sugary snacks and drinks between meals.

title: Tooth Sensitivity Treatment
description: Relief from sharp pain with cold, hot or sweet foods.
details:
Sensitivity usually comes from exposed root surfaces, worn enamel or gum recession. We find the cause and treat it with desensitising agents, fluoride varnish, bonding over exposed areas or advice on brushing technique.

Ideal for: Sharp pain with cold water or ice cream; Sensitivity after whitening or gum recession.

What happens: 1) Find the cause 2) Desensitising treatment applied 3) Bonding if root surfaces are exposed

Time: 20–30 minutes · Visits: 1–2 · Recovery: None

Aftercare: Use a sensitivity toothpaste; Brush gently with a soft brush.

title: TMJ & Jaw Pain Treatment
description: Care for jaw pain, clicking and teeth grinding.
details:
Pain or clicking in the jaw joint, headaches and worn teeth can come from grinding or clenching. Treatment may include a custom night guard, bite adjustment, exercises and advice to reduce strain.

Ideal for: Jaw pain or clicking; Morning headaches; Grinding or clenching at night.

What happens: 1) Joint and bite examination 2) Night guard impressions if needed 3) Fitting and review

Time: 30–45 minutes · Visits: 2–3 · Recovery: Gradual improvement over weeks

Aftercare: Wear your night guard as advised; Avoid chewing gum and very hard foods.

title: Prenatal Dental Care
description: Safe dental care for expecting mothers.
details:
Hormone changes in pregnancy can make gums swollen and prone to bleeding. Check-ups and cleanings are safe and recommended, and we plan any other treatment around the safest stage of pregnancy.

Ideal for: Expecting mothers; Bleeding or swollen gums during pregnancy.

What happens: 1) Check-up 2) Gentle cleaning 3) Plan for any needed treatment

Time: 30–45 minutes · Visits: 1–2 · Recovery: None

Aftercare: Rinse with water after morning sickness; wait before brushing.

title: Dental X-Rays
description: Low-dose digital X-rays for accurate diagnosis.
details:
X-rays show what can't be seen in the mouth — decay between teeth, infections at root tips, bone levels and the position of wisdom teeth — so treatment is planned accurately.

Ideal for: Diagnosing pain; Root canal and implant planning; Checking wisdom teeth.

What happens: 1) Positioning 2) Image taken in seconds 3) Results explained on screen

Time: 5–10 minutes · Visits: 1 · Recovery: None

Aftercare: Tell us if you are or might be pregnant.

title: Dental Consultation & Check-up
description: A full examination with clear advice and an honest plan.
details:
Your first visit includes a full examination of teeth, gums and bite, X-rays if needed, and a clear explanation of what we find. You'll leave with treatment options and costs explained before anything begins.

Ideal for: New patients; Second opinions; Anyone who hasn't seen a dentist in a while.

What happens: 1) Discuss concerns 2) Full examination 3) X-rays if needed 4) Options and costs explained

Time: 20–30 minutes · Visits: 1 · Recovery: None

Aftercare: Book any recommended treatment at a time that suits you.
